svg.text: Block parts $6.94 + 4-layer PCB $0.45 + JLCPCB assembly $1.20. CH32V307 does PoE PD, USB-PD source and networking (LLDP) via the switch.
Block parts $3.21 + 2-layer PCB $0.20 + JLCPCB assembly $0.70. Passive gigabit passthrough (MDI links are passive); CH32V203 does PoE PD + USB-PD only.
Notes: all costs USD @1k, LCSC/JLCPCB estimates (±30 %); block tags sum to each panel's parts total. Arrowheads show signal direction; ↔ = bidirectional.

The hot-swap NMOS is low-side: the MCU and its bootstrap supply sit on VIN−, while the load side (buck, USB-C, switch) has a switched ground, so MCU I/O to the load side stays idle until the FET is on.

Glossary: PSE = PoE power source · MDI = Ethernet line side · RMII/MDIO = MAC data / management bus · CC = USB-C config channel · Rp = source pull-up · BMC = USB-PD line code (TX via resistor divider,
RX via the MCU's on-chip op-amp as comparator) · TVS = surge clamp · 3V3_BOOT = tiny HV regulator, on above ~12 V, ≤ 4 mA during PoE mark events. 36–57 V is after cable drop and bridges.
